$comment: Machine-readable acceptance ledger (ТЗ 10/10 rev2 §22, §18.3). One entry per program milestone: status, requirement/evidence lists, blocking issues, waivers and the accepted commit. A milestone whose status is NOT 'accepted' must not be treated as a completed stage: downstream milestones may proceed only with evidence that this ledger records. No user consent, debug mode or high-risk grant can override a blocked requirement. Ordering gate (audit 'CI gate blocking M2 while M1.status != accepted'): a milestone may only be marked 'accepted' when EVERY earlier milestone is 'accepted'; scripts/check-milestone-gates.mjs --check enforces this in CI. A milestone whose works are shipped but whose predecessors are not yet accepted is recorded as 'in_progress' with a 'deliveredCommit'.

policy.comment: Strict sequential ordering: shipping work for a later milestone while a predecessor is not accepted fails the CI gate (scripts/check-milestone-gates.mjs). Formal acceptance additionally requires every earlier milestone accepted, an existing acceptedCommit in HEAD ancestry, empty or formally waived (non-P0) blockingIssues and non-empty evidence. The branch stops at the red stage: M2/M3/M4 deliveredCommit entries below are recorded as honest violations of this policy until their predecessors are accepted.

resolvedIssues: P0: session SecretStore destroyed legacy plaintext on bootstrap (FIXED in this milestone; portable/env flows verified in secretStore.spec.ts)
P0: plugin entrypoint inside signature/ escaped the signed digest (FIXED: validatePackage + host-side defense-in-depth)

P1: IPv6 link-local classifier only blocked addresses starting with fe80 while link-local is fe80::/10, and multicast ff00::/8 passed as public (FIXED: classifier now covers the fe80..febf hextet range and ff00::/8; memoryHost.test.ts pins febf::1 and ff02::1 as denied without a private grant, SEC-03)

P1: WebSocket handshake and incoming frame buffer lacked size/timeout limits — a declared huge frame could accumulate to full length before the bounded ring (FIXED: WS_MAX_FRAME_BYTES caps the declared payload and the fragmented-text accumulation; wsParseFrame answers tooLarge from the header alone and socketHandles tears the connection down; socketHandles.test.ts pins the 2-GiB declaration, SEC-04)

P1: networkPool did not decode gzip/br although the decompressed-bytes budget was claimed (FIXED: content-encoding gzip/deflate/br is decoded through a bounded streaming decoder — the compressed wire bytes and the decompressed result share the same cap, a gzip bomb cannot expand past it; networkPool.test.ts pins decode + header drop + bomb truncation, SEC-04)

P1: deleting a DB secret reference did not call SecretStore.delete (FIXED: SecretStoreHandle.deleteValue wired into the provider-secret and plugin-secret DELETE routes — the stored value is removed together with the referencing row, no orphaned secrets; secretStore.spec.ts asserts the value no longer resolves after delete, SEC-01)

P1: the whole signature/ directory was excluded from the digest — a signed entrypoint could import an unsigned signature/module.js (FIXED: verifyPackageTrust now recurses into signature/ and allows ONLY manifest.json + package.sig there; any other file in the directory is recorded with a forbidden sentinel so the strict file-set comparison rejects the package; packageTrust.test.ts pins the forged signature/module.js case, SEC-05)

P1: package digest was not re-verified at activation/startup and installs had no recovery journal (FIXED: install writes an installed-digests.json snapshot next to the promoted package plus a durable install-journal.json (staging→committed/rolled_back); every activation and the startup auto-activation re-verify the files against the snapshot and refuse with PLUGIN_SIGNATURE_INVALID TAMPERED_AFTER_INSTALL when anything was added/removed/modified; pre-upgrade installs get a baseline from the publisher signature; recoverInterruptedInstalls cleans half-promoted packages and .incoming-*/.rollback-* leftovers on boot; packageIntegrity.spec.ts 9 tests incl. end-to-end install→tamper→activate-refused, SEC-05)

waivers.issue: P1: profile export per-profile scoping (SEC-02 follow-up — the legacy single-app.db model has no per-profile foreign keys; per-profile scoping is a canonical-plane schema decision)
waivers.reason: Limited waiver per ТЗ Этап 1 exit criteria ('P1 either closed or covered by a limited ADR waiver until cutover'). SEC-02 is satisfied for the current model: the export is allowlist-only (entity + per-table column allowlist), snapshot-transactional and secret-redacted, and the legacy model holds no per-profile rows to leak — the selected profile is the whole data set. Per-profile scoping requires per-profile foreign keys in the canonical schema; tracked in M4 blockingIssues. Waiver expires at M4 cutover, when the canonical export must filter by profile.

prSplitPlan.note: Audit directive 'split the accumulated branch into security / kernel flow / migration / separate M4 PRs'. The branch history (main..HEAD) interleaves stages chronologically, so no single linear range is a clean topic. History will NOT be rewritten: after each milestone is accepted, its PR is cut by cherry-picking the listed commits onto main (conflict resolution against main is expected — the tail M1 commits were written against the accumulated tree). The strict sequential policy now prevents further stage mixing, so the branch stops growing.
